stem:
Meher looks at the diagram. Line $t$ crosses lines $p$ and $q$ at two different points, forming eight angles at those crossings.

Which claim correctly names the transversal and organises those angles?

options.text: Lines $p$ and $q$ are the transversal, and $t$ is only a third unrelated line.
Line $t$ is a transversal even if it meets only one of $p$ or $q$.
Line $t$ is the transversal because it meets both $p$ and $q$; the eight angles sit in vertically opposite equal pairs at each crossing.
The eight angles are what create transversal $t$ across $p$ and $q$.

teacher.key_rationale: A transversal must cut both of the other lines; $t$ does that and organises eight angles with vertically opposite equal pairs. Naming $p$ and $q$ as the transversal, dropping the both-lines condition, or reversing angles and transversal leave the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source parallel-line diagram as lines p and q cut by transversal t with eight numbered angles.
